Upgrades that make an older computer feel new again

A memory or storage upgrade often costs far less than a new computer and makes a bigger difference than people expect. We check what your machine supports first.

Book an upgradeSSD or HDD?

Upgrades we install

RAM

More memory for running several apps and browser tabs at once without slowdowns.

SSD

Replacing a hard drive with a solid-state drive is usually the biggest speed boost an older computer can get.

HDD

Large, affordable hard drives for desktop storage, archives, and backups.

Laptop batteries

A new battery when the old one drains quickly, will not hold a charge, or has swollen.

Power supplies

Desktop power supply replacement for failing units or new components that need more power.

Storage upgrades

Moving your files and system to a larger drive, so you keep everything you had.

Parts and labor, priced separately

You see exactly what you are paying for. Your quote lists the part and the installation as separate lines.

How an upgrade quote is structured
Quote lineWhat it covers
PartThe component itself, matched to your exact model. You can supply your own part if it is compatible.
LaborInstallation, data migration where needed, and testing afterwards.
DiagnosisConfirming compatibility and whether the upgrade will actually help.

Prices vary by device, part availability, and labor. We provide a written quote before any upgrade.

Will an upgrade help my computer?

Slow to start and open files

Usually storage. An SSD upgrade is often the fix.

Slows down with many tabs or apps open

Usually memory. Adding RAM helps if your model supports it.

Dies quickly off the charger

Usually the battery, which wears out with age and charge cycles.

Some computers cannot be upgraded

Many thin laptops have memory and storage soldered to the board. We will tell you if that is the case before you spend anything.

Find out what your computer can take

Send us the make and model. We will check which upgrades it supports and what difference they would make.
